explainer.subject: Chemistry
explainer.title: Why -NO2 makes Phenols more acidic

steps.say: It is tempting to think that because $-NO_2$ pulls electrons away, it makes the $O-H$ bond stronger or harder to break, which would decrease acidity.
Actually, acidity depends on the stability of the conjugate base. We need to see if the phenoxide ion formed is happy with its negative charge.
The $-NO_2$ group is an electron-withdrawing group (EWG). Through the ring, by resonance, it pulls the negative charge away from the oxygen and onto itself.
In chemistry, spreading out (delocalizing) a charge increases stability. Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize negative ions and thus increase acidity.
Because the nitro group at the para position stabilizes the phenoxide ion through both -I and -R effects, p-Nitrophenol is significantly more acidic than phenol.
Quick check: Does the substituent 'pull' or 'push'? If it pulls electrons away (EWG), it helps carry the negative charge 'burden', boosting acidity.

explainer.takeaway: Electron-withdrawing groups like nitro groups stabilize the phenoxide ion, making it easier for phenol to release a proton.
